output.review_comment: The ceil-based nearest-rank fix and the 0..100 range check are correct. Together they pass every test except `test_median_response_time`. The PR then adds a p=50 branch that averages the two middle values of an even-length list, and that branch exists only to make that one test return 135. It contradicts the docstring ("always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated") and the README ("every reported value is a real sample"). It also makes p=50 behave differently from p=49 and p=51, and it would put non-sample latencies in the dashboard's p50 through `latency_summary`. The PR description says averaging is what the SRE team agreed, but nothing in the repo supports that. The failing test conflicts with the documented spec: nearest-rank gives 120 for [80,120,150,200] at p50. No consistent implementation can pass it, so this should go back to the teammate and the SRE team to decide, not be hard-coded. Please remove the p=50 special case, keep the ceil fix and validation, and report the conflicting test. Minor: use `math.ceil(p * n / 100)` to avoid floating-point overshoot, e.g. p=7, n=100 currently gives rank 8.
